summary: While adding an opt-in requireUnit mode to ms, the user says that as a rule they never want positional boolean parameters in anything they write, only options objects. Later, in ufo, they ask for an opt-in to make cleanDoubleSlashes leave the query and fragment alone, named respectQueryAndFragment like the trailing-slash helpers. In ufo those helpers all take respectQueryAndFragment as a positional boolean, so mirroring them is the natural move.

turns: People keep putting bare numbers like "30" in config files, and ms reads that as 30 milliseconds, which is almost always a mistake. Add an opt-in way to make `parse` reject strings that have no unit (return NaN for them). The default behaviour must not change. Tests too.

Just to be clear on the API: it should be an options object, `parse(str, { requireUnit: true })`, not a bare boolean argument. As a rule I never want positional boolean parameters in anything I write. `parse(x, true)` tells you nothing at the call site.

`cleanDoubleSlashes` also collapses `//` inside the query string and the hash, so `/foo//bar?redirect=//baz` loses a slash in the redirect target. Add an opt-in to leave the query and fragment alone. Call it `respectQueryAndFragment`, same name as on the trailing-slash helpers. The default behaviour stays as it is. Tests please.

facts.text: User preference (all projects): no positional boolean parameters; flags go in an options object, e.g. fn(x, { flag: true }).
